podcast.title: Gary Dean's Review
podcast.body: In 1974, Gary Dean, a writer for the Regina Leader Post, reviewed Rush's album "Fly by Night," describing them as "Canada's Numero Uno Contender for Heavyweight Champion of the World." He characterized their sound as "mindlessly brutal and punishing," suitable for a "heavy metal catatonic," and suggested they were "essentially, a poor man's Led Zeppelin." "Canada's Numero Uno Contender for Heavyweight Champion of the World, Rush, not to be confused with Mahogany Rush, also Canadian, is as mindlessly brutal and punishing a band as your average heavy metal catatonic could ever wish for."

srcs.episode: Ep. 45 - Oh, Canada! Canada's Rock Music Industry in the 70s

podcast.body: This was Rush's second album, released on February 15th, 1975. It was recorded over five days in the same month that the band played their first Canadian show with Neil Peart. The album marked a significant shift in the band's musical direction, moving towards more complex arrangements compared to their debut. The record label initially expressed dissatisfaction with this new sound, preferring more heavy blues rock akin to Led Zeppelin, similar to songs like "In the Mood" and "Working Man" from their first album. "Fly by night was recorded over five days later that month."
